title: Dense disjoint irreducible opens inside a prescribed dense open
statement: Let k be a field, f:X → Spec k a separated finite-type curve of dimension at most one [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], and V a dense open. There are n and pairwise disjoint nonempty irreducible opens U_a inside V, indexed by Fin n, with dense union W, topological Krull dimension of X minus W at most zero [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and every connected component in W of a point of W is irreducible. This includes X empty and n = 0.

proof.text: Finite type over the field and quasi-compactness make X Noetherian. Index its finitely many irreducible components by I. For each component C_a let O_a be the complement of the union of all other components. This is open, and its closure is C_a; these are NoetherianSpace.finite_irreducibleComponents and closure_sUnion_irreducibleComponents_sdiff_singleton. Set T_a = V intersect O_a. Density of V makes T_a nonempty. It is an open subset of C_a, hence irreducible, and closure T_a = C_a. The sets T_a are pairwise disjoint.

Every point lies in some component C_a = closure T_a, so the union of the T_a is dense. Every point w of the closed complement specializes from the generic point z of a component containing w. Choose y in T_a. Since z specializes to y and T_a is open, z lies in T_a and outside the complement. Apply the proved source-library theorem topologicalKrullDim_lt_of_forall_exists_specializes to the complement inside X with d = 1 and dim X < 2. The result dim complement < 1 is dim complement at most zero by ENat.WithBot.lt_add_one_iff. This implements the dimension argument in Stacks 03SC without an additional postponed lemma.

For x in T_a, the connected component of x in the union is contained in T_a: T_a and the union of the other opens are disjoint open parts, and a connected subset meeting T_a stays in it. Conversely, irreducibility makes T_a connected, so it lies in that component. Their equality proves irreducibility of each connected component. Reindex I by Fin(card I). The empty case has no components and n = 0.

theorem exists_dense_irreducible_opens {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsCurve f] (V : X.Opens) (hV : Dense (V : Set X)) :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (U : Fin n → X.Opens),
      (∀ a, U a ≤ V) ∧ Dense (⋃ a, (U a : Set X)) ∧
      Pairwise (fun a b ↦ Disjoint (U a : Set X) (U b)) ∧
      (∀ a, IsIrreducible (U a : Set X)) ∧
      topologicalKrullDim ↥(⋃ a, (U a : Set X))ᶜ ≤ 0 ∧
      (∀ x ∈ (⋃ a, (U a : Set X)),
        IsIrreducible (connectedComponentIn (⋃ a, (U a : Set X)) x))

blueprint_update.statement: Let $k$ be a field, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ a curve [def-weil-pbc-curve-setting], and $V\subseteq X$ a dense open. There are $n\ge0$ and pairwise disjoint irreducible (in particular nonempty) opens $U_1,\dots,U_n\subseteq V$ whose union $W$ is dense in $X$, such that the complement $X\setminus W$ has topological Krull dimension at most zero, and the connected component in $W$ of every point of $W$ is irreducible. This includes $X$ empty and $n=0$.

proof.text: *The opens.* Since $X$ is of finite type over a field and quasi-compact, it is Noetherian; let $C_1,\dots,C_n$ be its finitely many irreducible components. Let $O_a$ be the complement of the union of the components other than $C_a$; it is open and its closure is $C_a$. Put $U_a=V\cap O_a$. Density of $V$ makes $U_a$ nonempty; it is an open subset of the irreducible space $C_a$, hence irreducible, with closure $C_a$. The sets $U_a$ are pairwise disjoint, since a point of $U_a$ lies on no other component.

*Density and dimension.* Every point lies in some $C_a=\overline{U_a}$, so the union $W$ is dense. Let $w\in X\setminus W$ and let $z$ be the generic point of a component $C_a$ containing $w$. As $z$ specializes to every point of $U_a$ and $U_a$ is open, $z\in U_a\subseteq W$. So every point of $X\setminus W$ is a proper specialization of a point outside $X\setminus W$, and since $\dim X\le1$, every chain of specializations inside $X\setminus W$ has length zero: $\dim(X\setminus W)\le0$.

*Connected components.* For $x\in U_a$, the sets $U_a$ and $\bigcup_{b\ne a}U_b$ are disjoint opens covering $W$, so the connected component of $x$ in $W$ lies in $U_a$. Conversely $U_a$ is irreducible, hence connected, so it lies in that component. Thus the component is $U_a$, which is irreducible. If $X$ is empty there are no components and $n=0$.
